title: She was born blind, raised by a grandmother who is deaf and mute - and became a Paralympian. October 4, 2026.
excerpt: From a 1977 speech that put Hindi on the UN's biggest stage, to a highway built with its own wildlife crossing, October 4's five stories are about people and institutions choosing to do things the harder, more honest way.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about choosing the harder path when an easier one was available - a minister speaking in his own language instead of English, a nonprofit leader redirecting her own award money, an airline co-founder spending his fortune on a hospital instead of a legacy wing with his name on a wall alone, a highway engineered around a forest instead of through it, and a blind girl who turned isolation into a Paralympic career.

October 4, 1977: India's External Affairs Minister became the first person to address the UN General Assembly in Hindi

Atal Bihari Vajpayee addressed the UN General Assembly's 32nd session entirely in Hindi, speaking on nuclear disarmament and invoking Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam - 'the world is one family.' It remains one of the only times Hindi has been spoken from the UN's main podium.

She leads Teach For India's US arm. In 2026, a new award named her its first-ever winner

Neha Gupta won the inaugural Deepak Raj Rising Star Award from the India Philanthropy Alliance, honoring an emerging Indian-American leader under 40. The $10,000 grant that came with it is going straight back into Teach For India US, the organization she has led since 2024.

An IndiGo co-founder is building a 500-bed hospital inside his old engineering college

Rakesh Gangwal, US-based co-founder of IndiGo Airlines, has committed Rs 400 crore total to build the Gangwal School of Medical Sciences and Technology at IIT Kanpur, including a planned 500-bed hospital and 200-bed cancer care research center - plus matching grants of up to Rs 300 crore to draw in other donors.

India built a highway with its own wildlife crossing - and the animals are actually using it

The Delhi-Dehradun Expressway, opened in April 2026, includes a 12 km elevated wildlife corridor through the Rajaji National Park region - and a follow-up camera-trap study documented 18 wildlife species, including elephants, already using it to cross safely.

She was born blind. Her grandmother, who raised her, is deaf and mute

Rakshitha Raju lost both her parents young and was raised in a remote Karnataka village by a grandmother who could not describe the world to her. A PE teacher at her blind school spotted her running ability; she went on to win gold at the Asian Para Games and World Para Athletics Junior Championships, and became the first Indian woman to compete in the T11 1500m at the Paris 2024 Paralympics.

Five stories, one thread: a minister who spoke in his own voice, a leader who gave her award back to her mission, a businessman who built a hospital instead of a monument, engineers who built around a forest instead of through it, and an athlete who ran through a world no one described to her. None of them took the easier path.
